subject: Request: Temporary "Service Safety Net" SLA for Novum's Beta Model Preview
messages:
From: Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@novumhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novum Health Procurement <procurement@novumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Beta launch — SLA ask and temporary commitments

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We’re planning to start a closed beta of our clinical triage assistant using Redwood’s new encoder-preview model on July 5. Because this model is still in preview, our internal legal/procurement team is pushing back on committing to your standard uptime SLA for the first 90 days.

To move forward, procurement asked whether Redwood can offer a temporary, formalized "service safety net" for the beta window:
- Reduced uptime commitment (we understand this may be lower than GA SLA)
- Explicit latency tolerance for p95 requests during the preview
- Defined credits and remedies if outages exceed the temporary threshold

Attached are the beta specs and a short risk summary for their review. Can you confirm if Redwood is open to this approach and what the proposed terms would look like? If possible, copy in anyone on your ops/product team who needs to be involved.

Best,
Sylvia Park
Director, Product Ops
Novum Health
[Attachment: novum_beta_specs.xlsx (Excel, 78 KB)]
[Attachment: beta-security-brief.pdf (PDF, 412 KB)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Beta launch — SLA ask and temporary commitments

Hi Sylvia —

Really appreciate the heads up and the docs. Short answer: yes, we can do a temporary, documented safety net for beta customers, but we need to align on concrete numbers and operational controls before signing anything. Proposed next steps from our side:

1) Draft a "Service Safety Net" addendum that:
   - States the duration (e.g., up to 90 days from beta start)
   - Defines a provisional uptime target (lower than GA) and latency p95 bounds
   - Specifies credit formula, incident reporting cadence, and rollback/fallback behavior

2) Loop in Marcus and Mina to confirm whether the preview model can be run with an automatic fallback to a GA-compatible variant and to enumerate risks (inference latency variance, KV cache warm-up, quantization delta).

3) Share SOC2/Security artifacts and a proposed notice period for decommissioning the safety net.

Can Marcus and Mina propose the provisional numbers by EOD tomorrow? I’ll start a draft addendum and share a link.

—Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: draft-service-safety-net-term.docx (Draft)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Beta launch — SLA ask and temporary commitments

Thanks for the tag, Priyom. High-level feasibility notes from the runtime/product side:

- Uptime: we can commit to a 95% availability target for the preview window (90 days). This reflects the added risk of experimental model variants and staging capacity constraints.
- Latency: recommend a provisional p95 target of 1.2s for typical 512-token requests; for longer sequences we should document expected degradation and provide percentiles.
- Fallback: we will configure an automatic fallback to the stable encoder-v1 model when the preview model exceeds latency thresholds or on infrastructure strain. Fallback is seamless at the API layer but may cause quality regressions.
- Monitoring & Runbooks: we'll provide a dedicated dashboard (token-level latency, error-rate, cache hit-rate) and an on-call escalation path with a 2-hour SLA for incident acknowledgement.

Risks: KV cache warm-up on new sessions can push p95 higher in early hours; aggressive batching during peak could amplify tail latency. Mitigations: prefix caching enabled, conservative batching config for the Novum tenant, and a 72-hour warm-up window where we monitor closely.

If Novum accepts those provisional numbers, we’ll finalize a short addendum and a joint runbook. Putting proposed terms here for visibility:
- Safety net duration: 2027-07-05 through 2027-10-02 (90 days)
- Provisional availability target: 95%
- Provisional p95 latency target: 1.2s (512-token baseline)
- Credit: service credit = 5% of monthly invoice for each 24-hour period below target, up to 30% cap for the month

We’ll need explicit sign-off from Novum procurement on the credits and on the rollback/fallback semantics.

—Marcus
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: (none)]

From: Novum Health Procurement <procurement@novumhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@novumhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 14:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Beta launch — SLA ask and temporary commitments

Priyom / Sylvia —

Thanks for the quick responses. A few points procurement needs clarified before legal will accept an addendum:

1) Credits: The proposed 5% per 24-hour period feels low for clinical usage. We need an agreement that scales credits with downtime severity (e.g., 5% for <24h, 15% for 24–72h, 30% for >72h) or an alternative minimum uptime guarantee during business hours.
2) Notice & Exit: We require a 14-day notice before Redwood can terminate or reduce the safety net protections.
3) Evidence: Please provide SOC2 report and the beta-security-brief (we received the brief but need attestation page uploaded).
4) Duration: Procurement prefers an initial 60-day pilot with option to extend — can we align contractually to allow extension with 7-day notice?

Can you confirm these points and send a redlined addendum?

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Director, Procurement
Novum Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <procurement@novumhealth.com>, Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Beta launch — SLA ask and temporary commitments

Camila / Sylvia —

Thanks for outlining procurement’s concerns. I’ve reviewed Marcus’s proposed operational controls and believe a formal "Service Safety Net" is the right path to de-risk Novum’s beta while enabling us to iterate on the preview model. Proposed reconciled terms from Redwood: 

- Pilot duration: 60 days starting 2027-07-05, with a single optional 30-day extension that either party can trigger with 7 days' notice.
- Availability target: 95% during the pilot window.
- Credits: tiered credit schedule — 5% for outages <24h, 15% for outages 24–72h, 30% for >72h, applied pro-rata to the affected billing period, up to a 30% cap.
- Notice & Exit: Redwood will provide 14 days' notice for planned reductions or termination of safety-net protections; emergency termination (security or regulatory) will be discussed with Novum but may be immediate.
- Latency: provisional p95 1.2s baseline for 512-token requests; documented degradations for longer inputs.
- Fallback & Quality: automatic fallback to encoder-v1 will be enabled; we will document expected quality deltas and surface a failback flag in the response metadata.
- Evidence & Security: SOC2 Type II attestation and the redacted beta-security-brief will be uploaded to the shared Drive link by EOD tomorrow.

Operational next steps: Priyom and Marcus will share a redlined addendum by EOB Friday and we’ll schedule a 30-minute joint runbook review next Monday. If Novum agrees to these reconciled terms, signatories on both sides can execute the addendum and we’ll begin the configured rollout on 2027-07-05.

I’ll be the executive approver for Redwood on this addendum. Thanks everyone for moving quickly.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[Drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C-novum-beta]
